relations.subject: Horace Hayman Wilson
relations.evidence: He studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital

relations.subject: Horace Hayman Wilson
relations.evidence: attached to the mint at Calcutta, where he was for a time associated with John Leyden

relations.subject: Horace Hayman Wilson
relations.evidence: superintended the studies of the Sanskrit College in Calcutta

relations.subject: Horace Hayman Wilson
relations.evidence: In 1832 Oxford University selected Wilson to be the first occupant of the newly founded Boden chair of Sanskrit

relations.subject: Horace Hayman Wilson
relations.evidence: In 1836 he was appointed librarian to the East India Company.

relations.subject: Horace Hayman Wilson
relations.evidence: He also taught at the East India Company College.

relations.subject: Horace Hayman Wilson
relations.evidence: On the recommendation of Henry Thomas Colebrooke, Wilson was in 1811 appointed secretary to the Asiatic Society of Bengal.

relations.subject: Horace Hayman Wilson
relations.evidence: original member of the Royal Asiatic Society, of which he was director from 1837 up to the time of his death.
